correctness.rationale: The proof specializes Oller-Marcén Proposition 6 to two fixed exponent primes, counts exact order classes in the cyclic group modulo the larger exponent prime, combines them with the smaller congruence by CRT, and applies the prime number theorem in fixed arithmetic progressions. The diagonal and finitely excluded primes contribute only O(pi(x)). A standalone finite replay found no discrepancy in 68448 admissible ordered prime pairs and verified the residue-class count for eight exponent-prime pairs. The finite replay is explicitly not used as proof of the asymptotic.
risks: The asymptotic depends on the exact specialization of Proposition 6 and on fixed-modulus prime equidistribution; finite computation alone would not establish either infinite statement.
sources: Standard prime number theorem in fixed arithmetic progressions

value.rationale: The exact constant measures how often integrality on a natural sparse family is produced locally versus by a cross-factor cyclotomic contribution. The positive-density compensation term is structurally motivated by Oller-Marcén's directed order condition and is invisible in the global density-one theorem. It supplies a quantitative invariant of the two-block interaction rather than an arbitrary finite slice or recomputation.
risks: The theorem is deliberately narrow to two fixed exponent primes and gives no secondary term or higher-block analogue.
sources: Oller-Marcén Proposition 6 supplies the natural cross-factor order condition whose distribution is quantified.
Bateman–Erdős–Pomerance–Straus global density results provide the contrasting full-integer baseline.
